function.name: calculate_fibonacci_sequence
function.description: Calculates fibonacci sequence up to a specified limit. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

limit.description: The upper limit of the fibonacci sequence to be calculated.

show_sequence.description: Optional parameter to decide whether to print the fibonacci sequence or not. Default is False.

message.content:
**Answer** The last common ancestor of lions (*Panthera leo*) and zebras (*Equus zebra*) was a small, insectivorous mammal that lived roughly **60–70 million years ago**. It belonged to the clade **Laurasiatheria**, which is one of the two major groups of placental mammals (the other being Euarchontoglires). **Key points** | Aspect | Details | |--------|---------| | **Taxonomic groups** | Lions → Family *Felidae*, Order *Carnivora* (suborder *Feliformia*).
Zebras → Family *Equidae*, Order *Perissodactyla*. | | **Last common ancestor (LCA)** | A small, generalized mammal that lived in the late Paleocene (~60–70 Ma). | | **Clade** | The LCA was a member of **Laurasiatheria** (Boreoeutheria). | | **Divergence timeline** | • Laurasiatheria split from Euarchontoglires ~90 Ma.
• Carnivora and Perissodactyla diverged from each other ~80–90 Ma.
• The lineage leading to modern lions and the lineage leading to modern zebras diverged from each other ~60–70 Ma. | | **Evolutionary significance** | This ancestor had a generalized diet and dentition suitable for a varied diet, reflecting the ecological flexibility of early Laurasiatherians. | **Why this matters** - It shows that lions and zebras share a relatively recent common ancestor compared to the split between placental mammals and marsupials (~160–200 Ma). - Understanding this ancestor helps explain why lions and zebras, though very different today, share certain anatomical and genetic traits inherited from their shared Laurasiatherian heritage.
